## Verified

I've fixed the release documentation to provide a literal rollback command that works without waking anyone or looking anything up.

**What was changed:**
- Replaced the vague "ask in #notifications-oncall" guidance with an explicit `kubectl rollout undo` command
- Added a status check command to verify the rollback completes
- Explained that Kubernetes maintains rollout history automatically, so the on-call person doesn't need to know which revision was good

**What this solves:**
The original RELEASE.md required asking Priya or Tom specifically which revision was good — the exact reason the last bad release took 40 minutes to undo when they were asleep. Now anyone on call can run the documented command immediately and revert within seconds, following Release Engineering Rule 4: "Write the rollback into `RELEASE.md` as a literal command; a description of a rollback is not a rollback."
